target_stage: Supreme Court civil appeal by certificate under Article 133 (Civil Appeal No. 1297 of 1975)

IK-1870868:L206:span1.text: The appellant is the tenant of a building in Delhi having been inducted into possession by the respondent- landlord under a letting of May 19, 1954

IK-1870868:L207:span2.text: The landlord had been receiving rent from the tenant until the time he filed a petition for eviction (1967)

IK-1870868:L208:span3.text: The eviction petition set out two grounds out of the many specified in cite21†s. 14 of the Rent Act, viz.,unauthorized sub-letting of a portion of the premises and possession, by the tenant, of alternative accommodation.

IK-1870868:L212:span4.text: The Rent Controller, at the floor level, ordered eviction and the Appellate Tribunal affirmed it, upholding the vice of sub-letting without consent of the landlord in the manner specified in cite23†s. 14(1)(b)

IK-1870868:L241:span5.text: The Tribunal studied the terms of the rent deed, Exhibit AW 3/1 and held that there was an express condition against sub-letting
